characters.why: Listing: 'mid-20s to 30s female', 'naturally calm, grounded delivery', 'raw, unfiltered Hinglish that sounds like a real person, not a script'. Age, register and the one behaviour the bible stresses (under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never louder) all match, and it is the only female listing that combines the right age with explicit Hinglish, the best English evidence the Hindi listing gives for the most English-mixed speaker. Preview median about 222 Hz: mid-range, clearly above Pushpa and the magistrate. Risks, untested: a support-bot voice may come out too even for 'quick, clipped'; [curt] and [deadpan] must supply the edge.
characters.backup_why: 'Young, direct', 'formal and to-the-point', 'without unnecessary emotion': the dry, clipped half of Nandini, also Hinglish. Same preview pitch (about 222 Hz), so it swaps in without upsetting the female pitch ladder. Weak point: built for IVR, so the s2e01 b12 quiet beat may sound like a policy read.

test_lines_note: Each character has 2 Hindi and 2 English listening-test lines under test_lines. Hindi lines are bible key lines or sample lines unless 'source' says 'S10 test-only line, not script'. English lines are the bible's sample_line.en where one exists; the rest are S10 renderings in the bible's voice_by_language register, for casting only. They are not script text: the episode writers' English supersedes them. Tags are eleven_v4 style; per the voice-direction skill, pass the text exactly as written, one line per call.

casting_notes.method: creative_list_voices with languages hi: 2 unfiltered pages of 30; filtered pages for female old (19), female middle_aged (30), male middle_aged (30), male old (20), use_case characters_animation (30), search 'Hinglish' (30), 'villain' (15), 'police' (15); plus languages en with accent indian (40) to look for voices listed in both. No voice in this cast appears in the English listing, and none of the en-indian voices appeared in the Hindi listing, so English support rests on listing text ('Hinglish', 'Hindi and English', 'bilingual') or nothing. Preview pitch: each preview downloaded, decoded to 8 kHz mono with ffmpeg, median f0 from a pure-Python autocorrelation (frames 40 ms, 70-400 Hz). Previews are 3 to 14 seconds of performed speech, so the figures are a rough guide only. For the three voices also measured in the proof cast, this method gave 163 / 190 / 174 Hz against the proof's 170 / 195 / 178, which is consistent.

casting_review.method: Local whisper.cpp (ggml-small, no prompt, no script; ggml-base as a third opinion on four cuts) and ffmpeg (silencedetect, ebur128 true peak and LUFS, a pure-Python voiced-frame and pitch tracker with YIN cross-check). Full per-take figures in content/series2/casting/review.json. No speech generated, no connector transcription.
